attributes.body_ja:
「こそ」は、名詞（または名詞句（めいしく））を強調（きょうちょう）するために使（つか）われる副助詞（ふくじょし）です。これに接続助詞（せつぞくじょし）の「から」が付（つ）くと、「理由（りゆう）」を強調（きょうちょう）するときの表現（ひょうげん）になります。

「からこそ」は、主（おも）に動詞（どうし）や名詞（めいし）のあとに付（つ）けて使（つか）われます。名詞（めいし）と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）う場合（ばあい）は、名詞（めいし）のあとに「だ」に付（つ）けて、「だからこそ」という形（かたち）にします。

「からこそ」は、いろいろな理由（りゆう）がある中（なか）で、特（とく）に大事（だいじ）な理由（りゆう）を強調（きょうちょう）したいときに使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
Traditionally, the adverbial particle こそ is used to emphasize whatever noun (or noun phrase) it is attached to. However, when combined with the conjunction particle から, it focuses on emphasizing the 'reason' for something. This structure is very similar to phrases like 'precisely because (A)' in English.

からこそ is an expression that is primarily used after either verbs or nouns. In the case of nouns, the noun will need to be followed by the auxiliary verb だ, before からこそ is added.

With からこそ, there may be several reasons for why something is the way it is, but こそ will show that there is a 'foremost' reason that should be considered before anything else.

attributes.source: A Handbook of Japanese Grammar Patterns

attributes.description: 接続・意味・使い方・例文

attributes.body: あまり follows a noun or verb phrase and shows that an extreme state leads to an unintended result, e.g. 緊張のあまり声が出なかった ('I was so nervous I couldn't speak.') からこそ attaches after the reason and emphasizes it as the precise cause, e.g. 緊張したからこそ全力を出せた ('It was precisely because I was nervous that I gave it my all.')

からこそ and ことだから are similar in that both can emphatically state a reason. However, ことだから is typically used to make a prediction or assumption based on a person's known behavior or character, e.g. 田中さんのことだからできると思う ('Because it's Tanaka, I think he can do it'). In contrast, からこそ is more broadly used to emphasize a specific reason, e.g. 努力したからこそできた ('I could do it precisely because I worked hard').

Both からこそ and ～てこそ emphasize cause and effect, but they differ in nuance. からこそ highlights a specific reason with a strong emphasis, e.g. 努力したからこそ合格できた ('I was able to pass precisely because I worked hard'). In contrast, ～てこそ indicates that only after a certain condition is fulfilled can something else happen, e.g. 努力してこそ意味がある ('It only has meaning after putting in effort').

second_relatable.title: ～てこそ
second_relatable.meaning: Only if, Because, By, Unless, Until

attributes.body: からこそ and ものだから are similar in that both can be used in expressing a reason. They differ in that からこそ is used to specifically emphasize the reason, like saying 'it is precisely because of (A) that (B)', while ものだから is not as emphatic, and is generally used when providing an explanation or excuse for one's actions or a situation.

Despite appearing different, ～ばこそ and からこそ are essentially synonymous in meaning, both expressing an reason for something, i.e. 'it is precisely because of (A) that (B)'. The main difference is that ～ばこそ is a highly formal and literary expression found primarily in writing, while からこそ is far more common and used in everyday speech as well as writing.

first_relatable.title: ～ばこそ
first_relatable.meaning: Precisely because, Only because, Because, Due to, Only if

attributes.body: Both use こそ for emphasis, but からこそ highlights a reason or cause, meaning 'precisely because', e.g. 努力したからこそできた ('I could do it precisely because I worked hard.'). こそ on its own emphasizes the word it follows, framing it as precisely the one, e.g. 彼こそできる ('He, if no one else, can do it.')

second_relatable.title: こそ
second_relatable.meaning: For sure, For certain, Even more so, Underlined or bolded text

attributes.body: から expresses a reason or cause, similar to 'because of A, B' or 'A, so B' in English. The reason comes before から, with the result after. からこそ is the same から followed by the emphatic こそ, highlighting that the given reason is precisely or solely responsible for what follows. It's used for strong arguments or emphatic points.
